facts: The machine interface is everything a program observes when calling ocx: JSON documents, the error document, exit codes, OCX variables and command grammar. [L9]
Every document written by --format json has one object shape at its top level, never a bare array, string or number. [L15]
A root is an object, and its schema_version comes first as an integer naming that root's shape. [L17]
Absent means unset: an optional field without a value is left out, and null never stands for unset. [L20]
Under --format json, stdout holds exactly one pretty-printed JSON document per invocation, including after a usage error. [L24]
schema_version appears in every report root and the error document, while contract reports every document and command version in one object. [L39]
A program can read contract once and refuse to run any command whose version it does not support. [L42]
A version increases when a property, root, enum value or variant is removed, renamed, retyped, or a flag or exit code changes. [L44]
Additions such as new properties, roots, enum values, commands or flags do not change a version. [L51]
A contract ledger records each break, and a gate refuses a break missing from the ledger or from the version bump. [L53]
Enum values and union variants are open, so a later release may emit a value the program has never seen. [L57]
An unknown status is not success, so checks compare against known success values and fail closed. [L60]
An unknown union variant is skipped rather than guessed, based on its type key. [L61]
Every invocation ends in a report with exit 0, a report followed by non-zero exit with no error document, or an error document. [L67]
A batch with one missing package writes its full report and exits with the decisive failure code, never two concatenated JSON values. [L75]
A zero exit code with a status that is not a known success value is still a failure for the program. [L77]
A command that fails without a report prints one error document, including refused command lines and invalid OCX variables or config. [L81]
error.message is human-readable text that is not stable, so a program must never match on it. [L104]
Branch on error.kind for the family and error.detail for the cause, since a detail slug is stable once a release emits it. [L107]
Under --quiet a failure still prints the error document, and a --format json after a bare double dash belongs to the child. [L109]
Exit codes follow sysexits for the standard categories 64 to 78, with 79 to 82 for ocx-specific cases, and are stable across releases. [L113]
Exit 75 means a rerun may succeed while exit 69 means it will not, so a wrapper can loop on one and stop on the other. [L117]
Exit 81 is a deliberate local refusal from offline, frozen or user-edited shell profiles, not a fault. [L118]
Exit 82 means the registry, forge or build lacks the capability, so rerunning never helps. [L119]
A child process run by ocx exec forwards its own exit code unchanged. [L121]
Each document is described by a JSON Schema published on the site for validation or type generation. [L125]
Published schemas allow unknown properties and encode open values as strings with a documented list of known values. [L132]
